The foreman is a **manual-scheduling mode, said honestly**: one interactive
session replaces the pi orchestrator's spawn/poll/relay loop with its own
judgment, launching single-item workers, reviewing their work, sending it
back, and landing it itself. It uses the toolkit's supported surfaces
(`herdr_delegate.py watch` / `answer`, `dev_status.py`) instead of ad hoc
scripts and raw `send-keys`. When you want the hands-off scheduler instead,
use `/swarm` — the two are deliberately separate, and this skill points at
`/swarm` rather than re-deriving its decisions.

## 1. Preflight

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

Fails? Say you are not running inside herdr and stop. Do not fall back to
anything, and never drive the UI-focused pane.

### Known limitation: Claude Code's own auto-mode classifier

When **this session itself** is a Claude Code session running in Auto Mode,
every `herdr agent start` invocation can be denied by Claude Code's own
auto-mode classifier — a second, undocumented gate that runs *after*
`permissions.allow`, which does **not** bypass it. The denial observed on
2026-10-14 was not an `agent start` but a `git merge --ff-only` plus
`git push origin main` in the foreman session, which went through only after
the operator granted it in-session. On any denial, ask the operator once, then
retry the identical command; never route around it (for example by having a
worker merge instead — the foreman lands, never the worker). Pi has no
equivalent classifier, only its allowlist-based `permission-gate.ts`.

## 2. Scheduling by hand

Eligibility comes from `dev_status.py`, never from this skill's guesswork:

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/dev_status.py ready --prefix <prefix>
```

Only `worker_safe: true` items are eligible, because `launch --slug`
enforces a worker-safe prefix (`check_launchable`). `serial_safe`-only items
go to `/swarm --serial`, never to the foreman. Launch one item per worker:

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/herdr_delegate.py launch --slug <slug> --kind pi [--model <model>] [--handoff]
```

- **Set acceptance before launch** — before `launch --handoff`, set the
  item's contract acceptance:
  `python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/dev_status.py acceptance-set <slug> '{"criteria": [{"text": "...", "refs": [{"repo": "<main checkout root>", "path": "<repo-relative path>", "clause": "<clause>"}]}], "independent_verifier": true}' --if-rev <rev>`
  — criteria drawn from the repo's written contract (AGENTS.md/README/
  PROJECT_PLAN.md), each citing the clause it covers; `independent_verifier:
  true` when a non-worker verifier must gate-pass. The command prints the
  token-file path (`<data dir>/verifier/<slug>.token`). Keep that path
  **private** — never put it in item notes, feedback files, or worker
  prompts; a worker that holds it is the verifier and self-grades.

- **When to prefer `/swarm`** — a hands-off run with concurrency and file-
  overlap headroom handled by `selectSchedulable` is `/swarm`'s job, not
  yours. The foreman only overrides overlap for read-only reference files, by
  editing the item's `related_files` (which the scheduler also reads).
- **Unblocking and splitting blockers** — keep slots full. Unblock a
  dependent by completing its blocker, then launch it. Split a blocker that
  is really several independent items into new backlog items (`dev_status.py
  add`), with rationale recorded.
- **De-overlapping `related_files`** — two items naming the same file are
  never spawned together (each worker gets its own worktree, the second merge
  would conflict). For read-only reference files, edit the item's
  `related_files` so the scheduler no longer defers the pair.
- **Preinstalling sudo-only deps** — pi's `guard-rails.ts` blocks `rm -rf`
  and `sudo` outright; a worker that genuinely needs them is stuck. Preinstall
  any such dependency yourself before launching the worker.
- **Per-worker exclusive resources** — assign ports (e.g. GDB/emulator ports)
  or GPU ids per worker so concurrent workers never collide.

## 3. Watching

Do not poll by hand. Run this in the background and let the settle wake you:

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/herdr_delegate.py watch <agent>... [--prefix <prefix>] --state <state-file> --timeout-s <n> [--grace-s 60] [--poll-s 15] [--strict]
```

It is **level-triggered** with explicit acknowledgement: it reports an agent
whose status is `blocked`/`done`/`idle` and whose `state_change_seq` differs
from its acked seq, plus any member that has gone from the listing, and exits
0. Reporting never acknowledges — pass `--ack <name>=<seq>` / `--ack-gone
<name>` only *after* you have acted on a report, so a crash before acting
re-reports the same event. Exit 124 means timeout with nothing to report. The
limitation to know: it reports current state only, so a transient block that
resolved before a poll is not reported — for a settle you cannot afford to
miss, lower `--poll-s`.

## 4. Review checklist

Before landing or sending back, check every claim against the repo's written
contract (its AGENTS.md / STYLE.md / acceptance criteria) and raw run outputs:

- **Criteria vs contract** — each gate criterion the worker claims is covered
  by a clause in the written contract, not a weaker self-written one.
- **Claims vs raw output** — a "verified"/"passing" claim is checked against
  the actual command output, not the worker's summary.
- **Negative control present and non-circular** — a check that can only pass
  if the defect is real, not a tautology.
- **Numbers copied from real output** — counts, timings, and hashes come from
  the run's own stdout, not re-derived.
- **No slugs in tracked files, no `/tmp` provenance** — a backlog slug must
  not leak into a committed file, and ad hoc scripts live outside `/tmp`.
- **Re-run the tests yourself** — run the suite (or the relevant subset)
  again rather than trusting the worker's report.

## 5. Send-back

Write the feedback to a file outside any repo
(`~/.agent-toolkit/data/foreman/<slug>-feedback-<n>.md`), then drive the worker's
picker to the free-text entry:

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/herdr_delegate.py answer <agent> --expect-pane <pane> --other --text "Foreman review: read <path> and act on it"
```

`--text` is a short pointer, not the payload (≤120 chars, printable ASCII,
single spaces). Exit code handling: 0 ok; 3 means needs_manual with nothing
sent (safe to retry); 4 means needs_manual *after* navigation or text was
sent — inspect the pane before acting; 5 means submitted but the picker
persisted (unconfirmed).

## 6. Landing

Launch with `--handoff` (see step 2): the worker runs `land` through its
commit step, then stops **before** the merge/push/cleanup gate and prints a
single line:

```
FOREMAN-HANDOFF slug=<slug> branch=<branch> commit=<sha> worktree=<path>
```

The foreman lands, never re-entering `land`: rebase onto the **merge target**
(the default branch, or the item's declared `integration_branch` when one is
set — `release-1` work merges into `release-1`, never main), re-run the suite,
fast-forward merge, push, remove the worktree, delete the branch. Before
gate-pass, run
`python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/dev_status.py contract-touch <slug> --repo <path> --range <merge-base>..HEAD`
after the rebase (and re-run it against the merge target) so any
contract-file change in the branch — including earlier commits and anything
the rebase introduces — is caught. Then record `dev_status.py run` evidence,
`gate-pass <slug> '{"coverage": {...}}' --verifier-token-file <path>` (pass
the token-file path, never the token value), `review`, and `approve`. Read the
worker's digest offers from
`~/.agent-toolkit/data/foreman/<slug>-digest.json`, relay them to the operator,
and delete the file after relaying. Last, once `approve` has marked the item
done, close the worker's tab — every time, unprompted:

```bash
python3 ~/.agent-toolkit/scripts/herdr_delegate.py close <agent> --expect-pane <pane>
```

`<pane>` is the pane from the launch JSON. It refuses, closing nothing,
unless the item is done, the agent is idle or done, and the tab holds only
that worker's pane. Never close at the FOREMAN-HANDOFF line: a send-back
still needs the live worker. A classifier denial goes to the operator once
(step 1); `--force` waives only the item and status checks and is the
operator's call. Without `--handoff`, worker behaviour is unchanged.

## 7. When to ask the operator

Ask, never decide alone: public or outward actions, taste gates, spend
increases, destructive actions, and any auto-mode classifier denial (see
step 1). Commit and merge/push approvals belong to the operator **unless the
operator has explicitly delegated them to the foreman for this run**; in that
delegated mode the foreman owns the review-and-landing approvals itself. A
foreman run that was not given that delegation must stop and ask.

## 8. Relationship to `/swarm` and the pi orchestrator

The foreman is a **mode, not a second scheduler**. It does not re-implement
the pi orchestrator's decisions in prose: eligibility comes from
`dev_status.py ready`, launch from `herdr_delegate.py launch --slug`, and the
hands-off run from `/swarm`. `swarm_spawn`/`swarm_poll`/`swarm_resolve_blocked`
(`pi/extensions/swarm-tool.ts`) keep owning spawn, poll, blocked-relay and
amend for pi; the foreman drives a worker's picker with `answer` instead. See
the `backlog-item` skill for the per-item procedure the worker runs, `land`
for the gates the foreman's handoff takes over, and `swarm` for the hands-off
alternative.
